To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single base pair germ-line mutation was found in the p53 tumor suppresor gene in a family with an aggregation that includes adrenocorti cal carcinoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, breast cancer, and osteosarcoma.
a germ-line p53 deletion was identified in a Li-Fraumenii-like family with a high aggregation of adrenals tumors.
a single base pair deletion in codon 215 of the p53 germline was found in two affected members of a cancer predisposed kindred.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the p53 tumour suppressor gene.
the molecular genetics of human cancer and the development of molecular diagnostic tools for the detection and identification of cancer susceptibility genes.
the study of genetic predisposition to cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deletion of a single base pair in codon 215 of the p53 is a germ-line mutation and is associated with the aggregation of adrenocoical carcinoma, rhdomyosarcoma and osteosarcoma.

a germ-line deletion of the p53 codon 215 in the Li-Fraumenie syndrome family described in the present study is associated with the development of a spectrum of tumors, including adrenocortial carcinoma, rhabdosarcoma, osteoarcoma, and breast cancer.
this is a family with a germ-line p53 mutation that predisposes to cancer, but that this mutation does not define a specific tumor type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a germ-line mutation in the p53 tumor-suppressor gene is associated with a predisposition to cancer in a family with an aggregation that includes rhabdomyo-sarcoma.
the single base pair deletion is the second germ-line p53 mutation found in a Li-Fraumenie family.
this family is a new member of Li-Frauman syndrome, and that this family is the first to have a p53 deletion in the germ-line DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spectrum of tumors observed is not necessarily a function of the type of p53 mutation.
the denaturing gradient gel method used here is a powerful technique for screening large families with cancer aggregation for mutations of the highly conserved regions of the p53 coding sequences.
the spectrum of tumors observed among families with germ-line mutations of the p53 genes is very similar.
